{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABeQrPlA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhHxnx0", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 275, "title": "Capture Web dictation microphone on the current page and stream PCM to extension ASR without a permission tab", "body": "## Goal / approved implementation decision

Replace the existing **extension-owned microphone permission setup tab** with **microphone capture initiated directly from the original Web page**. Stream live audio to the extension-owned existing local-ASR graph runtime. The original page's mic button remains the only recording control.

**Implement the new architecture end-to-end in this Issue. This is not a feasibility-only spike or a proposal.**

Expected UX:
1. Focus a supported input field on an eligible HTTP(S) website; the existing mic icon appears when Web microphone is ON and a compatible graph exists.
2. Click mic → call `getUserMedia({ audio: ... })` in a suitable context on **that page**. If needed, Chrome displays its native **site-scoped** microphone prompt for the current page; permission is not obtained from a disposable extension tab.
3. Once allowed, record immediately and stream normalized audio to the **existing extension-hosted local ASR/graph**. Committed text goes to the same original field.
4. Click the same mic to Stop (or Cancel while preparing), with final drain, cleanup, and original-field protection.
5. **Do not open a new permission tab, extension popup/window, side panel, or additional UI** for this workflow. Do not silently fall back to the old one-time setup tab when a page forbids microphone capture.

The user **accepts per-website mic permissions**. The user does **not** accept extra visible setup tabs or windows.

## Implementation

- In `extension/web-voice-content.js` or a narrowly scoped page-side capture adapter, acquire the media stream as part of the user's explicit mic-button gesture, in a context where Chrome associates permission with the **current website**. Respect HTTPS/secure context and the site's Permissions Policy/CSP; if blocked, report a clear, local error rather than opening any extra tab.
- Use Web Audio (prefer AudioWorklet where compatible) to produce **mono 16 kHz PCM**, with short bounded chunks (e.g. 50–100 ms to start; tune based on measurements). Forward chunks using a **document/session-scoped authenticated Chrome extension messaging channel** to the offscreen runtime through the coordinator, preserving sequence numbers and order. Keep audio local: no server/network upload.
- Pick an efficient transport supported by the browser version and the current MV3 message serialization rules. Prefer typed-array/binary transport where actually supported; if serializing to JSON/base64 is necessary, explicitly measure CPU, memory, message volume and latency. Do not claim zero-copy or assume Chrome always supports transferable ArrayBuffers through `chrome.runtime.Port`.
- Put only microphone capture and lightweight audio normalization on the page; **reuse** `TabSession`, `MicrophoneAudio` graph path, model cache, Workers, VAD/ASR, field output and graph-selection/eligibility logic **inside the extension-owned runtime**. The PCM source adapter should feed the existing graph port; do not fork ASR models, modify user graphs, or add a parallel transcription engine.
- Do not let arbitrary website scripts forge start/stop/audio/output messages or observe raw audio through a newly exposed page-world channel. If a page-world bridge is unavoidable, explicitly authenticate and minimize it, and acknowledge its trust boundaries; do not expose model or transcript contents to page scripts beyond the intended text-field insertion.
- Ensure bounded buffering/backpressure, cancellation, stop/drain semantics and late-chunk rejection. Close the microphone track and AudioContext/Worklet on Stop, Cancel, permission revocation, page navigation/removal, target invalidation, Web OFF, connection loss, runtime crash or extension reload. Keep per-page/document ownership and concurrent independent Live + Web sessions.
- Remove the old permission-only tab workflow (`extension/web-voice-permission.html/.js` and associated `permission-needed`/`permission-ready` setup handshake) when no longer used. Update docs, tests, error strings and permission semantics accordingly, without unrelated UI changes.
- Reference the repo's earlier page-audio relay in `extension/page-agent.js` (selected media capture/PCM messaging from #81 / PR #82) and browser examples researched: Say, Pi (page capture path), Voice Message Transcriber (content → SW → offscreen PCM transfer). Reuse relevant concepts, not obsolete/slow conversion code by default.

## Non-blocking post-merge user verification — explicitly approved

**The owner will personally test the installed extension after this PR is merged. Manual/physical-device/native-browser confirmation must NOT block implementation review, PR approval, merge, Issue closure, or Project Done status. Do not request manual results before merging and do not create a separate blocking Issue just for manual verification.**

Complete this Issue with implementation, normal code review and **feasible automated tests**. Report exactly what the tests exercised. Do not claim that manual website permission bubbles, specific external sites, or a physical microphone were verified when they were not.

After merge the owner will check real-world permission UX and transcription; any observed regressions can be reported then as follow-up bugs.

## Acceptance criteria (automatable where practical)

- [ ] Existing in-page mic starts capture with the current page's browser-native permission flow, with **zero new extension tabs/windows**; first grant and already-granted cases are covered.
- [ ] Current site owns its mic decision. Denied/blocked site permission, Permissions Policy restriction, unsupported context and hardware errors produce actionable feedback without opening an extension setup page.
- [ ] PCM is streamed continuously in order to the **existing** local ASR path; original field receives exactly-once finalized output, with correct caret/target and no submit.
- [ ] Start/Stop/Cancel, rapid click, pending permission prompt, long sessions, page focus changes, navigation, tab close and revocation release the correct mic and runtime resources.
- [ ] Multiple Web tabs and Live windows continue to operate independently; one mic control does not launch two graphs concurrently.
- [ ] Representative transport measurements are recorded: capture-to-runtime delay and jitter, CPU/memory or serialization overhead, throughput/backpressure and dropped/late chunks under ordinary and busy-page fixtures. No unacceptable real-time regression vs current offscreen capture in the measured fixtures. State the actual environment and limitations.
- [ ] Automated Chrome/MV3 tests cover first-use grant/denial, no-extra-tab behavior, PCM-to-ASR integration, session isolation, graceful drain and resource cleanup. Use native APIs and controlled microphone/ASR fixtures; do not claim to have clicked Chrome's native permission bubbles if not actually done.
- [ ] Docs match the new architecture. No new permanent controls, generic trigger configuration, Graph Library redesign or unrelated changes.

## Related

- #263 / PR #264: old setup-tab + offscreen-mic design being replaced.
- #247: original Web mic capability.
- #266: left-click run/stop, right-click choose default graph; preserve behavior.
- #265: reusable subgraphs and eligibility.
- #267: multiple independent Live windows; preserve concurrent execution.
- #273: mic position simplification; unrelated to audio transport.

## Scope discipline

**User-approved behavior only.** Do not add dashboard settings, a new permission workflow screen, transport debug UI, optional speech providers or speculative features. If platform limits prevent this architecture on some websites, preserve clear failure handling and record limitations, but do not reintroduce the permission tab as a hidden fallback.
